title: Cyberspace explorer
description: The parts of the page, which is one HTML file: what the reader sees, how a repository is read, how views are drawn and written, and the services it reaches from the reader's browser; and the Worker in worker/ that serves it and signs readers in with GitHub; and the crawler in crawler/, a second Worker that collects what the explorer shows of websites and of repositories without views.

components.name: Screen
components.responsibility: Everything the reader sees: a bar across the top, a status line, a column of folders and the folder being read, with panels that open over it.

components.name: Bar
components.responsibility: The strip across the top: the brand (a link to the landing page), the repository and its ref, the Flat / Cyberspace switch (offered where WebGL works), the Tokens button and Choose another repository.

components.name: Landing page
components.responsibility: Shown when no repository is given: a headline, what the browser does, the address field, an example repository and a tile for each kind of view.

components.name: Status line
components.responsibility: One line under the bar saying what is happening (listing, reading), what went wrong, or what was skipped, with at most one button for the one thing worth doing about it.

components.name: Folder column
components.responsibility: The filter, the Waiting link and the tree of folders that have .dev files, each with small icons for the kinds of view it holds.

components.name: Folder view
components.responsibility: One folder: its crumbs, name and purpose, the folders inside it as chips, a tab per kind of view and the open tab's content.

components.name: Inspector
components.responsibility: A panel at the right that holds everything a drawing says about the selected part, with its neighbours as links; in Cyberspace a floating card with the same body.

components.name: Token panel
components.responsibility: A small dialog under the Tokens button: the tokens kept, a field for a new one, what it is for, and whether to keep it after the tab closes.

components.name: Waiting view
components.responsibility: Every open decision and blocker in the repository, as two tables linked to the records.

components.name: Repository reading
components.responsibility: Turns an address into the repository's .dev files, from the reader's browser.

components.name: Address parser
components.responsibility: Splits an address into a host, a repository, a ref and a folder; anything not on github.com is tried as GitLab.

components.name: GitHub adapter
components.responsibility: Lists a GitHub repository's files and reads them, through the API with a token or from raw.githubusercontent.com without.

components.name: GitLab adapter
components.responsibility: Lists a GitLab project's files, a hundred to a page, and reads them through the GitLab API.

components.name: Workspace adapter
components.responsibility: Lists and reads the views a host page hands over in window.cyberspaceWorkspace (the VS Code extension's workspace folder), with no token and no ?url=.

components.name: Crawler adapter
components.responsibility: Lists and reads the views the crawler made of a website, through the Worker's /api/space, and tells the Worker a player approached the address so stale data is rescanned.

components.name: Loader
components.responsibility: Finds the .dev/*.json files under the folder asked for (or, where the root has a .cyberspace-explorer folder, the files in it, and nothing else), reads twelve at a time, keeps the views and knowledge files it knows and sorts each folder's files by kind.

components.name: Token store
components.responsibility: Keeps the reader's tokens by scope (a host, an owner or group, or one repository) in this tab or this browser, and picks the narrowest one around a repository.

components.name: Router
components.responsibility: Reads the part of the address after # and shows that folder, part, view, record or the Waiting view; with ~space as its last segment, Cyberspace.

components.name: Drawing
components.responsibility: Turns diagrams, use cases and journeys into SVG drawings the reader can pan, zoom and click through.

components.name: Diagram models
components.responsibility: Turns each kind of drawn view into parts, clusters and lines with their tooltips and inspector content: component, deployment, class, state, use case and user journey.

components.name: Layout
components.responsibility: Places the parts with dagre, makes room for cluster headers, packs separate pieces into rows and smooths the lines, keeping dagre's own points on each line for Cyberspace's floor traces.

components.name: Renderer
components.responsibility: Writes the drawing as SVG: plates, clusters, lines, arrowheads, labels and the grid of crosses behind them.

components.name: Part interaction
components.responsibility: Lights a part's neighbours on hover, shows tooltips, selects a part into the inspector and grows a part into the page when it opens another folder.

components.name: Camera
components.responsibility: Fits a drawing to its width, and pans and zooms it with a drag, the wheel with ⌘ or Ctrl, a pinch or the buttons in its corner.

components.name: Written views
components.responsibility: Cards for capabilities, features, use cases and journeys, the table of operations, and each view's full tables, related views and sources.

components.name: Knowledge renderer
components.responsibility: Groups a folder's knowledge files as the catalogue does and shows each record as a card: badges, summary, safe Markdown, every field, origin, relationships, sources and links.

components.name: Cyberspace
components.responsibility: The second way in: the repository in 3D, under a black-to-indigo sky on a glossy black floor, in place of the folder column and view; always dark, whatever the theme switch, the system or a host says, with the whole window in the page's dark colours while it shows, and the theme switch disabled. A folder opens as a tower of glass floors, one per .dev file, with a drawn view pulled out and its city small on it; entering that floor flies down into the city, and Esc flies back up. A drawn view stands as a city of cyan glass towers with glowing edges in its kind's colour and magenta beacons on the flat layout's ground plan, every relationship a glowing circuit trace on the floor between pads at the parts' bases; clicking a tower, plate or beacon selects it, lights its traces in place and raises them as beams, brightens its neighbours' pads, opens the inspector on it and puts it in the address. Above the towers, a repository with several folders is a skyline of buildings, one per folder, that the reader rises to and flies into. A city can stand other drawn views of its folder beside it. Opened by an address whose last segment is ~space; without WebGL 2 or three.js it says why and Flat shows instead.

components.name: Stage
components.responsibility: The WebGL renderer, scene and camera, in Cyberspace's palette read once (spaceTheme): a sky sphere round the eye and a glossy floor, fog in every material, unlit premultiplied glass (teal at a tower's base to cyan at its roof), and every edge a glow line drawn with its own falloff, no post-processing; multisampling only below a pixel ratio of 2. Stands a city's meshes (instanced glass plates, towers and beacons; one set of glow lines, beacons' uplinks among them; and one geometry of flat ribbons on the floor, blended by their maximum, holding every trace with the bright run where it arrives, every pad, a final state's second ring, a start point's ring and dot and the selection's dashed ring, recoloured in place as the selection and the pointer change: 3 to 5 draw calls a city, and the lit beams' core and glow while a part is selected) or a folder tower's (the floors as one instanced glass mesh, their rims and the rails as glow lines, their faces as one set of lines and one of tiles, and the pulled-out floor as a drawer with its glow, its ghost slot and its city scaled down) on the floor, or every city standing in a city scene, side by side, or the skyline's buildings (their floor slabs and shells instanced, their edges and slab outlines one set of glow lines, and the lines to parent folders as traces with every building's pad one geometry of ribbons: six draw calls with the sky and the floor), finds what is under the pointer (a part by its glass, a trace where the ray meets the floor or a plate's top, a lit beam by a hidden tube), slides floors out and back, fades the tower out behind the city that takes its place and in again, and out as the skyline fades in and back, fades an unticked city to dim before it goes, draws a frame only when something changed and none while hidden, follows the window's size, times each frame to the GPU's finish with a pixel read back under ?spacestats, lets go of the scene on leaving and of the context a minute later, and offers Restore it when the context is lost.

components.name: World builders
components.responsibility: Turn a drawn view into a city in world units, from the layout Flat draws it with (or a grid without one): groups as plates, parts as towers as tall as their beams make them, a component's or deployment's outside services as beacons, start points as rings with a dot, and every edge as a circuit trace on the floor, routed along the points dagre gave it in the flat drawing, squared off, in lanes where traces share an avenue, slid clear of towers and up and down plates' walls, between pins on pads at the parts' bases (and as an arc while it is lit, those between the same two parts fanned out); find the trace under a point of the floor. Turn a folder's files into a tower of floors in three groups (drawn, written, knowledge), each floor with what its top shows: a drawn view's plan from its city, a written view's cards as bars, a knowledge file's records as lines. Turn the repository's folders into a skyline: a building per folder on the radial tree of folders, each subtree given the angle its buildings need, the rings widened until they fit, a floor per file in its tower's order, each folder's line to its parent a trace square to the rings, siblings in lanes. Place the cities standing side by side, each 12 units right of the last, and join them into one world to walk in and map. Pure functions, tested in Node; built once per view and direction, once per folder, and once for the skyline.

components.name: Camera rig
components.responsibility: The camera in orbit, pan and walk modes: fits the city into the room the panels leave, with the projection centred on it, and turns, pans and flies with a drag, the wheel, a pinch, the arrow keys, + and −, and F, within limits. In the tower it takes the design's opening pose, framed in the whole window and climbed for a stack taller than 24 floors, and the wheel climbs; it flies between the tower and a city, and between a city and its street, on an arc, at once with reduced motion. In the street it walks: it puts the eye 12 units from a part across the layout's flow, looking up at it, then moves it with W A S D, the arrows, Space and Z at a pace that doesn't depend on the frame rate, turns it with Alt and a drag, slides it along towers, steps it onto plates and keeps it within the city's bounds grown by 30; the city's lit beams are drawn at 0.28 of their radii while it walks. In the skyline it opens 6.25 rings from the address folder's building, 24° up, framed in the whole window, and Fit everything shows every building; it flies between the skyline and a tower. A camera the reader hasn't moved fits again, over 300 ms, to everything standing when a city is stood beside the others or taken away. It turns toward what the reader selects: in a city the point it turns about glides to the part's middle, which comes to the centre of the room the inspector leaves, distance and angles kept; in the street the eye turns where it stands to face the part, for 250 ms and 3 more a degree, at most 700; in the tower it climbs to the floor selected. Each glides as a flight does, without the arc, stops at the reader's input and is at once with reduced motion; clearing the selection moves nothing. A part, floor or building focused from the keyboard out of view or under a panel is brought just inside the room: across the ground in a city and the skyline, by turning the eye in the street, by climbing in the tower, as ↑ and ↓ go from floor to floor. The street's walking keys work wherever the focus is but where they mean something else: W A S D and Z but in a text field, the arrows and Space on the canvas or with nothing focused. A flight that lands at once, with reduced motion, is never left as the trip under way.

components.name: Labels
components.responsibility: HTML labels over the canvas: a pill for each part, cut at 150 px, with Flat's badge or the step's glyph, and each plate's name with its number of parts; placed nearest first, pushed clear of each other and off the panels, with leaders, and faded out with distance. By a tower: each floor's kind and title left of its slot, and a bracket for each group with its name and count. With several cities standing, each label belongs to its city and its part. Over the skyline: a pill per building, its folder's title and last segment, for the address folder, its ancestors, the folders two levels below it and the one under the pointer, at any distance. A label the canvas's edge would cut slides inside it, by at most half its width, or is hidden.

components.name: HUD
components.responsibility: The panels over the scene, in Cyberspace's own colours (--space-panel, --space-rule, --space-pill, --space-hot) over the page's dark ones: over a city, the camera controls (orbit, pan, walk, zoom in and out, fit everything) and the legend, worded for the kind of view; over the tower, the folder's card (its name, path, purpose, counts of drawn, written and knowledge files, and the folders inside it) and the pulled-out floor's (its view, what its city holds, Enter the city and Slide back); in the street, in place of the city's, the breadcrumb (folder, view, plate and the part selected or ahead), the key hints, the map (plates, the traces as hairlines with the selection's lit, towers, beacons and the eye with its view cone; a click flies the eye there), the hover card by the part under the pointer (never under the inspector), a crosshair and a vignette. Over a city, the Layers panel on the left: the folder's views by kind, a tick box for a drawn view with a city of its own, radio buttons for a file's use cases or journeys, written and knowledge views listed but disabled. Over the tower, See the skyline, and the folders inside folded into a chip that opens it. Over the skyline, the address folder's card with what the repository holds and Enter <its title>, the camera controls with Walk off, the legend, and the street's hover card by a building, clear of the folder card. From the keyboard: a visually hidden list after the canvas, a button per part, floor or building, named after it, which Tab walks in the order of the flow and which lights what it names and does what a click does on Enter; and, per scene, what the scene shows and how to move in it, for screen readers. The Layers panel disables a view whose city would take the scene past 40 draw calls; below 1280 px wide it folds into a 40 px button that opens it as a popover, and the legend shows its icons alone.

components.name: Dock
components.responsibility: Cyberspace's left edge: Back, Forward, History, bookmarks, and a button per kind of drawn view that draws it in neon over the blurred scene; its parts lead there through the warp.

components.name: Theme switch
components.responsibility: System, Light or Dark in the bar, for Flat: sets html[data-theme] before the first paint and whenever the choice or the system changes, keeps a choice in localStorage, and hides when a host owns the theme. Cyberspace is always dark: its buttons are disabled while it shows.

components.name: Icons
components.responsibility: The page's own icon set on a 24-unit grid, and the rules that pick a component's icon from its name.

components.name: Sign-in and my repositories
components.responsibility: On the landing page: asks the Worker whether it signs readers in, offers Sign in with GitHub (or, without the Worker, a pasted GitHub token), and fills the address box's drop-down with the reader's repositories.

components.name: Worker
components.responsibility: Serves the page at cyberspace-explorer.com, signs readers in with GitHub and reads GitHub for them with their token, which never reaches the page.

components.name: VS Code extension
components.responsibility: Shows this page in a VS Code webview for a workspace folder, hands it the folder's views and the editor's theme, and opens the files it links to.

components.name: Crawler
components.responsibility: cyberspace-crawler, a second Worker: keeps the list of repositories and websites to explore, scans them on a schedule or on request, and stores what the explorer needs to draw them.

components.name: dagre 3.1.3
components.responsibility: The graph layout library, loaded from jsDelivr. Without it every view is shown as tables.

components.name: three.js 0.187.0
components.responsibility: The 3D library, core only, loaded from jsDelivr on first entry to Cyberspace. Without it Cyberspace says so and Flat shows.

components.name: Barlow typefaces
components.responsibility: Barlow, Barlow Semi Condensed and Barlow Condensed, loaded from jsDelivr; system fonts stand in without them.

components.name: GitHub
components.responsibility: api.github.com and raw.githubusercontent.com: the repository's tree and its files.

components.name: GitLab
components.responsibility: gitlab.com or a self-hosted GitLab that allows the page's origin: the repository tree and raw file endpoints.

components.name: Browser storage
components.responsibility: sessionStorage and localStorage in the reader's browser, where tokens are kept.
